sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Shift in Political Methodologies**: **Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education, and Passive Resistance** became central points of contention and debate within INC sessions between 1905 and 1916.
• **The Moderate-Extremist Ideological Divide**: Moderates aimed for **colonial self-government** through constitutional methods, while Extremists demanded **Swaraj** (complete self-rule) through mass action and direct confrontation with British imperialism.
• **Institutional Captures & Venue Politics**: The choice of session venues often dictated the balance of power between the Moderates and Extremists, culminating in the **Surat Split of 1907**.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: 1905 (Banaras) to 1916 (Lucknow) represents the cycle of radicalization, expulsion, isolation, and triumphant reconciliation of the nationalist movement.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: President: Gopal Krishna Gokhale. Held in U.P. Condemned the Partition of Bengal.
Extremists wanted extension of Swadeshi & Boycott to the whole of India; Moderates wanted it restricted to Bengal.
Prelims: Marks the formal entry of Extremist resolutions and testing ground for Tilak vs Gokhale.
President: Dadabhai Naoroji. Held in Bengal. Four historic resolutions passed.
Dadabhai Naoroji's towering stature prevented a split. Resolutions on Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education, and Swaraj.
Prelims: First time the word 'Swaraj' was officially adopted from the Congress platform.
President: Rash Behari Ghosh. Venue shifted from Nagpur to Surat (Extremist stronghold).
Clash over venue, presidential candidate, and dilution of Swadeshi/Boycott resolutions by Moderates.
Prelims/Mains: The infamous 'Surat Split'; Extremists (Lal-Bal-Pal) expelled; Congress dominated by Moderates until 1914.
President: Ambica Charan Mazumdar. Re-entry of Extremists into the INC.
Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Home Rule League pressure + Tilak-Jinnah Pact (Lucknow Pact).
Prelims/Mains: Historic Congress-League Pact and reunion of Moderates and Extremists.

items.definition: Adopted officially at the 1906 Calcutta session. For Extremists, it meant complete autonomy and freedom from foreign control, distinct from colonial self-government.
A weapon of economic pressure targeting British Manchester cloth, Liverpool salt, and British-made goods to revive indigenous industries.
A procedural deadlock engineered by Moderates to disqualify Tilak from contesting the presidency, leading to physical scuffles, police intervention, and the split of 1907.
An agreement reached between the INC and the Muslim League in 1916 accepting separate electorates, which significantly shaped communal politics and nationalist unity.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Maharashtra & Bengal Belts**: Focal points of Extremist radicalism led by Tilak, Aurobindo Ghosh, and Bipin Chandra Pal.
• **Venue Shift Politics**: Shifting sessions from Nagpur (Extremist favorable) to Surat (Moderate favorable) in 1907 illustrated spatial manipulation of internal party democracy.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Repression by the colonial state (Deportations, Sedition Acts) and the decade-long political vacuum caused by the Surat Split.
• **Policy Interventions**: The 1916 reunion proved that mass agitation combined with institutional negotiation yielded greater leverage against the British.

items.title: Mnemonic for Extremist Phase Presidents (1905-1907)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "God Dad Ran"
• **Decoded Meaning**: **G**okhale (1905 Banaras) -> **Dad**abhai Naoroji (1906 Calcutta) -> **Ran**k/Rash Behari Ghosh (1907 Surat).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls the exact sequence of presidents during the most volatile years preceding the split.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 1905 = Protest, 1906 = Demand (Swaraj), 1907 = Split, 1916 = Reconnection.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that the word 'Swaraj' was first used or coined at the 1906 Calcutta Session. False. The term was first used by Dadabhai Naoroji or Dayanand Saraswati earlier, but 1906 marked its first official *adoption* in an INC presidential resolution.

Mains Value Addition: Analyze the Surat Split not merely as an ego clash, but as an inevitable structural friction between two distinct political trajectories: petition-based liberalism versus mass-mobilization nationalism.

keyTakeaways: The 1905-1917 INC sessions trace the transition of the national movement from moderate elite lobbying to radical mass-based assertion.
The Calcutta Session (1906) and Surat Split (1907) define the high-water mark of ideological polarization and state suppression.
The 1916 Lucknow Session successfully reversed the 1907 split and cemented Hindu-Muslim political alignment through the Lucknow Pact.
